title: Create Cannabis Population Indicators — create_cann_pop
text: Creates binary population indicators based lifetime, last year, /last month substance use variables. function generates columns indicating whether individuals ever used, used past year, used past month. Users can specify indicators create.

title: Create Cannabis Population Indicators — create_cann_pop
Create Cannabis Population Indicators — create_cann_pop
text: dt data.table data.frame containing substance use variables. types character vector specifying indicators create. Must contain one : "ltp" (lifetime), "lyp" (last year), "lmp" (last month). Default c("ltp", "lyp", "lmp") create three indicators. order content types must match order content vars. vars character vector containing variable names corresponding types. types = "ltp", provide 1 variable (lifetime use) types = c("ltp", "lyp"), provide 2 variables (lifetime, last year) types = c("ltp", "lyp", "lmp"), provide 3 variables (lifetime, last year, last month) Variables coded 1-2 indicate use. value character string use suffix created variables. Default "cannabis".

title: Create Cannabis Population Indicators — create_cann_pop
text: data.table additional columns based types: ltpPop_{value} Lifetime population indicator (1 = ever used, 0 = never) lypPop_{value} Last year population indicator (1 = used past year, 0 = ) lmpPop_{value} Last month population indicator (1 = used past month, 0 = )

title: Create Cannabis Population Indicators — create_cann_pop
text: function creates cascading indicators: Lifetime (ltp): 1 lifetime use variable 1 2 Last year (lyp): 1 last year variable 1-2, lifetime variable 2 Last month (lmp): 1 last month variable 1-2, last year variable 2, lifetime variable 2 cascading logic means: create "lyp", must also include "ltp" types create "lmp", must also include "ltp" "lyp" types

title: Create Cannabis Population Indicators — create_cann_pop
text: input data.table copied avoid modifying reference. Missing values handled FALSE (coded 0) conditions.

title: Create Cannabis Population Indicators — create_cann_pop
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ library(data.table)  # Create sample data dt <- data.table(   id = 1:5,   lifetime_use = c(1, 2, 3, 1, NA),   year_use = c(1, 2, 3, 2, 1),   month_use = c(1, 3, 3, 1, 2) )  # Create all three indicators (default) result <- create_cann_pop(   dt = dt,   vars = c("can1", "can6", "can10"),   value = "cannabis" )  # Create only lifetime indicator result <- create_cann_pop(   dt = dt,   types = "ltp",   vars = "lifetime_use",   value = "cannabis" )  # Create lifetime and last year indicators result <- create_cann_pop(   dt = dt,   types = c("ltp", "lyp"),   vars = c("lifetime_use", "year_use"),   value = "cannabis" )  # With different substance result <- create_cann_pop(   dt = dt,   types = c("ltp", "lyp", "lmp"),   vars = c("can1", "can6", "can10"),   value = "mdma" ) } # }

text: d data.table data.frame. input dataset. types character vector specifying population types calculate. Options "ltp" /"lyp". Default c("ltp", "lyp"). vars named unnamed character vector variable names corresponding types. named, names match types. unnamed, order match order types. val character string used suffix created variable names. New variables named ltpPop_<val> /lypPop_<val>. ans character string specifying name answer/response column dataset ltp drug question. Default "ans1".

title: Create Population Indicators for LTP and LYP Variables — create_narko_pop
text: function creates population indicators based following logic: LTP: Value 1 LTP variable 1 2, LTP missing answer variable ans1 equals 2. Otherwise 0. LYP: Value 1 LYP variable 1 2, LYP missing LTP equals 2, LYP missing answer variable ans2 equals 2. Otherwise 0.

title: Create Population Indicators for LTP and LYP Variables — create_narko_pop
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ library(data.table)  # Create sample data dt <- data.table(   id = 1:5,   ltp_var = c(1, 2, NA, 3, NA),   lyp_var = c(1, NA, 2, NA, NA),   ans1 = c(1, 1, 2, 1, 2) )  # Calculate both LTP and LYP populations result <- narko_pop(   d = dt,   types = c("ltp", "lyp"),   vars = c("ltp_var", "lyp_var"),   val = "2024" )  # Calculate only LTP population result_ltp <- narko_pop(   d = dt,   types = "ltp",   vars = "ltp_var",   val = "2024" ) } # }

text: dt data.table. input data.table object containing age variable. var Character string. Name age variable categorized. breaks Numeric vector. Default TRUE. validate Logical. input validation performed? Default TRUE. copy Logical. copy data.table returned instead modifying place? TRUE object name different name. Common age groupings demographic analysis include: Pediatric: 0-18 years Young adult: 19-30 years Middle age: 31-50 years Older adult: 51+ years breaks vector always include minimum expected age (often 0) maximum value exceeds highest age data.

text: Survey data often uses special numeric codes represent different types missing responses: 999: "know" 998: "Prefer answer" 997: "applicable" -1, -9: Various missing codes missing_values parameter allows specify codes, converted NA age categorization. ensures survey response codes interfere legitimate age values properly treated missing data resulting age groups. validate=TRUE, function checks : Existence specified age variable Numeric age variable Proper breaks vector (numeric, sorted, minimum length 2) Matching labels length (provided) Coverage valid age values breaks (excluding missing codes) Valid missing_values parameter (provided)

title: Categorize Age Variable into Groups — group_age
code: library(data.table) #> Warning: package 'data.table' was built under R version 4.5.2  # Create sample data dt <- data.table(   id = 1:100,   age = sample(18:80, 100, replace = TRUE),   gender = sample(c("M", "F"), 100, replace = TRUE) )  # Basic usage with automatic labels age_breaks <- c(0, 18, 30, 50, 100) dt_grouped <- group_age(dt, "age", breaks = age_breaks, copy = TRUE)  # With custom labels age_labels <- c("Youth", "Young Adult", "Middle Age", "Senior") dt_custom <- group_age(dt, "age",                        breaks = age_breaks,                        labels = age_labels,                        new_var = "age_category",                        copy = TRUE)  # With missing value codes (common in surveys) dt_survey <- data.table(   id = 1:100,   age = c(sample(18:80, 90, replace = TRUE), rep(999, 5), rep(998, 5)) )  # Handle survey missing codes dt_clean <- group_age(dt_survey, "age",                       breaks = c(0, 18, 30, 50, 100),                       labels = c("Youth", "Young Adult", "Middle Age", "Senior"),                       missing_values = c(998, 999),  # "no answer", "don't know"                       copy = TRUE) #> Found 10 observations with missing value codes that will be converted to NA.  # Check the result table(dt_clean$age_group, useNA = "ifany") #>  #>       Youth Young Adult  Middle Age      Senior        <NA>  #>           0          16          26          48          10
